title: Cancellation and Refund of a Road Hazard Protection Certificate
content:
## Terms
**C1.** A Road Hazard Protection certificate can be cancelled by its holder at any time while active, and a pending certificate is voided when its tire set is cancelled.

**C2.** The cancellation is the holder's own decision: the agent registers the request and the holder confirms it.

**C3.** The certificate must be in status active when the holder's cancellation is completed.

**C4. Refund basis.** The refund is chosen by the first rule that applies, in this order:
1. *Void before install* — a pending certificate whose set was cancelled is refunded its full price.
2. *Covered set returned* — an active certificate whose covered set was returned under the satisfaction trial is refunded its full price.
3. *Full-refund window* — a cancellation completed within the plan's full-refund days of the purchase date, counted in calendar days from the day after the purchase date, on a certificate with no claim number at all, is refunded its full price.
4. *Pro rata* — otherwise the refund is the certificate price (the price per tire multiplied by the number of tires covered) multiplied by the whole calendar months remaining from the cancellation date to the expiration date (a partial month not counted), divided by the plan term in months, rounded half up to the cent, less the plan's administration fee, less the benefits already paid on the certificate (its replacement, out-of-area reimbursement and roadside service amounts) when the plan deducts benefits paid, and never below 0.00.

**C5.** The refund goes to the tender that paid for the certificate.

**C6.** Remaining roadside calls lapse with the certificate.

## Terms retired in part
The scope below is a holder's cancellation of an active Crestline Road Hazard Life-of-Tread Protection certificate bought in cash, by debit card or on a bank credit card that falls to the pro-rata basis (no void-before-install, covered-set-returned or full-refund-window refund applies).
- **C2** is **no longer in force** for a Life-of-Tread cancellation in that scope: there the holder confirms in person and the cancellation completes at once. Every other cancellation stays under C2.
- **C4, rule 4 (pro rata)** is **no longer in force** for a cancellation in that scope, which is refunded on the Life-of-Tread cancellation refund. Every other cancellation that falls to the pro-rata basis — a Life-of-Tread certificate bought on the Crestline card or charged to a fleet account among them — stays under rule 4, as do every void and every other refund basis.

## Full-refund window boundary (hypothetical)
Certificate purchased September 1, no claim number on it, 30-day window: a cancellation completed October 1 is refunded in full; one completed October 2 falls to the pro-rata basis.

## Pro-rata example (hypothetical)
Certificate price 100.00 (4 tires at 25.00), 24-month term, 10 whole months remaining, administration fee 20.00, benefits paid 12.50: 100.00 multiplied by 10 and divided by 24 is 41.666..., rounded to 41.67; less 20.00 and less 12.50 the refund is 9.17. Had the benefits paid been 30.00, the result would be held at 0.00.

superseded_clauses: The cancellation is the holder's own decision: the agent registers the request and the holder confirms it.

pro_rata: otherwise the refund is the certificate price (price_per_tire times covered_tire_count) times hazard_msr_unexpired_months divided by coverage_term_months, rounded half up to the cent, minus cancellation_admin_fee, minus hazard_msr_benefits_paid when refund_reduced_by_claims is true, and never below 0.00.
